entities.summary:
Bertold von Henneberg-Römhild (1442–1504) was a pivotal figure in the tumultuous era of the Holy Roman Empire.


As Archbishop of Mainz and Prince-elector of the Empire from 1484, he played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political landscape of Western Europe during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. His efforts to reform the Catholic Church and promote the Protestant Reformation had far-reaching consequences for the course of European history.



Bertold von Henneberg-Römhild's leadership of the reform faction within the Empire led to the establishment of the Electoral College, a powerful institution that would influence the political destiny of Germany for centuries to come.



His tenure as imperial chancellor from 1486 underscored the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the politics of the Holy Roman Empire during this period.




As leader of the reform faction, Bertold von Henneberg-Römhild played a pivotal role in shaping the religious and political landscape of Western Europe during the late 15th and early 16th centuries.




This figure's legacy continues to be felt in the modern era, as the Protestant Reformation's impact on European society and culture remains a defining aspect of the continent's identity.
